transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

No, it is not safe to keep using your tumble dryer. You should stop using it immediately.

A burning smell from a tumble dryer is almost always caused by lint buildup, which is highly flammable and a leading cause of household fires. In rare cases, it could indicate an electrical fault or overheating motor.

### ✅ Immediate Steps to Take:
1. Turn off and unplug the dryer immediately.
2. Do not use it again until it has been inspected and cleaned by a qualified technician or you have performed a thorough cleaning yourself (if comfortable).
3. Check the lint filter: Remove it and clean it thoroughly. Even if it looks clean, residue can build up in the ducting.
4. Inspect the exhaust vent/hose: Lint often accumulates in the flexible hose behind the dryer or at the external wall outlet. This is a common fire hazard. Use a vacuum with a hose attachment to remove lint from the vent path.
5. Look for signs of damage: Check for melted wires, scorch marks, or unusual noises when it was running.

### 🚨 When to Call a Professional:
• If you’ve cleaned the lint filter and exhaust vent but still smell burning.
• If the smell persists after cleaning.
• If you see smoke, sparks, or visible damage.
• If the dryer feels excessively hot to the touch on the outside.

### 🔥 Why This Is Dangerous:
Lint is composed of tiny fibers from clothing that are highly combustible. When combined with heat and restricted airflow (due to clogged vents), it can ignite easily. According to fire safety organizations, failure to clean lint filters and exhaust ducts is a primary cause of dryer fires.

Safety first: It’s better to spend time cleaning or calling a repair technician than risking a house fire. If you’re unsure about cleaning the vent system yourself, hire a professional appliance repair service.

ok I switched it off at the wall after the 2nd time?? the lint filter was really full, not cleaned for a few weeks. the hose behind is squashed and I can see fluff inside the end of it. is that what's causing it??

Yes, absolutely. That combination — a very full lint filter, a squashed hose, and visible fluff buildup inside the vent path — is almost certainly what’s causing the burning smell.

Here’s why:

### 🔥 What Happened:
1. Lint Buildup: When the lint filter isn’t cleaned regularly, it becomes less effective at trapping all the fibers from your clothes. Excess lint escapes into the dryer’s internal ducting and exhaust hose.
2. Restricted Airflow: A squashed or kinked hose severely restricts airflow. Hot, moist air can’t escape properly, causing the dryer to overheat.
3. Overheating + Lint = Fire Hazard: Lint is highly flammable. When it accumulates in a hot, poorly ventilated space (like a crushed vent hose), it can smolder or even ignite — producing that burning smell.

### ✅ What You Should Do Now:
1. Leave the Dryer Off until you’ve fully cleared the blockage and inspected everything.
2. Straighten or Replace the Hose:
• If it’s a flexible foil or plastic hose, replace it with a new rigid metal vent hose (safer and more durable).
• Make sure it’s not kinked, crushed, or too long (keep runs under 8–10 feet if possible).
3. Clean the Entire Vent Path:
• Detach the hose from both the dryer and the wall outlet.
• Use a vacuum with a long nozzle attachment to suck out all loose lint from:
     • The dryer’s exhaust port
     • Inside the hose
     • The wall vent duct
• If possible, use a specialized dryer vent cleaning brush kit for a deeper clean.
4. Clean the Lint Filter: Wash it with warm soapy water every time you dry clothes (lint isn’t just removed by brushing — residue builds up over time).
5. Check the Dryer’s Internal Ducting (if accessible): Some lint may have entered the dryer itself behind the filter housing. Wipe it out carefully with a vacuum or damp cloth.

### 🛡️ Going Forward:
• Clean the lint filter before every load.
• Vacuum or brush the vent hose and wall outlet every 3–6 months (more often if you run the dryer frequently).
• Inspect the exhaust hose annually for damage, kinks, or buildup.

### ⚠️ When to Call a Professional:
If after cleaning you still smell burning, notice scorch marks, see melted plastic, or hear unusual noises when restarting, stop using it and call an appliance repair technician. Electrical faults or internal component overheating could also be at play if the vent wasn’t the only issue.

You caught this early — great job! Fixing the airflow restriction will likely solve the problem completely.
